sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page vaoo1237 and reference records (Tryon 1976; Lynch & Crowley 2001; classification comment citing Lynch 2016a, 2016b, 2019)
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology listed for Vao (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology). ELAR search facets for Malekula show no Vao deposit; PARADISEC/OLAC pages were blocked (an automated-access block / connection refused) so archive holdings could not be checked.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2019. The phonological history of Nese, a Northern Malakula language. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 37: 61-82.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE Nese (Northern Malakula subgroup = Malua Bay, Nese, Botovro, Vovo, Vao). sec. 2.1 p.62: 'Stress is generally penultimate' (Nese, after Crowley 2006/Takau 2016). sec. 5 p.~75 argues final-vowel loss in the subgroup is 'compatible with a situation in which stress occurred regularly on the penult'. Vao appears only in comparative data columns; no synchronic Vao stress statement.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2014. Unexpected final vowel retention in Malakula. Open Linguistics 1(1): 1-16.

sources.note: Open-access companion to Lynch 2011 on final vowels across Malakula (stress-conditioned); publisher site refused automated download, needs a browser download.

sources.note: Survey entry only: sources are Hagen & Pineau 1888 ('Fooa' vocabulary), Guy 1974b, Tryon 1976 wordlist, Maddieson 1989 (linguolabials), Catechism 1900. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Capell, A. & John Layard. 1980. Materials in Atchin, Malekula: Grammar, Vocabulary and Texts. Pacific Linguistics D-20. Canberra: ANU. (CC BY-SA online edition, sealang/CRCL)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NEIGHBOUR LANGUAGE Atchin (urip1239), not Vao. sec. 1.3 Accentuation pp.14-16: accent partly lexical/historical but 'The tendency to penultimate accent is generally stronger than the tendency to keep the accent where it was in the original word'; enclitics draw accent forward so penultimate accentuation is maintained. Vao is mentioned only for linguolabials (p.7) and noun reduplication (p.13); no Vao accent statement.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1976. New Hebrides Languages: An Internal Classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL6211.N44 T7
sources.note: Vao = wordlist 102 (p.177ff) in broad phonetic transcription with NO stress marks (checked visually, p.177); sound-correspondence tables list Vao reflexes only; p.75 states no phonemic analysis was attempted. Silent on Vao stress.

sources.citation: Layard, John. 1942. Stone Men of Malekula: Vao. London: Chatto & Windus. (archive.org IGNCA scan, scanned full text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnography with a Vao glossary. p.25 phonetics note covers only linguolabial articulation and s>h, g>gh; no stress rule. One incidental remark p.366 (Low Maki): the sledge name 'vet simbe-simbe with the accent shifted on to the penultimate e'. Glossary (pp.747ff) has no accent marks. Index entry 'Phonetics 25, 218-19' confirmed: nothing on accent there.
